sets.relationshipLabel: a tradesperson and the structure or system their work is about
sets.explanation: Each tradesperson is defined by the specific structure or system their labor produces or maintains.

sets.relationshipLabel: a household signal and what it announces
sets.explanation: Each device exists solely to signal one specific event to the people inside the house.

sets.relationshipLabel: a category of home/roof and a specific style within it

glossary.definition: A style with steep sides that slope down on all faces, often with small windows poking out near the top.

definitions.definition: A skilled worker who builds things out of brick or stone, laying each piece by hand.
A solid upright structure that divides space or holds a building up.
Someone trained to safely install and fix the electrical systems in a building.
The network of electrical cables running through a building, carrying power to outlets and lights.
A little button-and-chime setup that lets someone at the door let you know they're there.
A person who's come to see you or stop by your place.
A small device on the ceiling that shrieks when it senses smoke, warning you of danger.
Flames and heat from something burning, either useful for warmth or dangerous when out of control.
Any place where someone lives, from a tiny cabin to a big house.
A cozy, low house usually all on one floor.
The covering on top of a building that keeps rain, sun, and snow out.
A style with steep sides that slope down on all faces, often with small windows poking out near the top.
The ceremonial first dig that marks the start of building something new.
The tearing down of a building, often on purpose and sometimes with a big crash.
The final meeting where paperwork gets signed and a property officially changes hands.
The moment you make the last payment and finally clear a debt completely.
